topic: Sharp common-binary-confounder ATE bounds and tipping frontiers for the Rosenbaum–Rubin odds model. For finite categorical X and binary A,Y,U, assume consistency and (Y(0),Y(1)) independent of A conditional on (X,U). In each stratum bound OR(A,U) in [1/Gamma_A,Gamma_A] and OR(Y(a),U) in [1/Gamma_a,Gamma_a], with interior observed p=P(A=1|X) and r_a=P(Y=1|A=a,X). Let w_a=P(U=1|A=a,X), pi=p w_1+(1-p)w_0, and D_A be the compact cross-product-odds region. For fixed r,w,pi and theta=OR(Y(a),U), derive the unique feasible root of (1-w)(theta-1)mu_0^2+[1+(w-r)(theta-1)]mu_0-r=0, set mu_1=theta mu_0/[1+(theta-1)mu_0], and use q-r=(pi-w)(mu_1-mu_0) to prove outcome extrema occur at theta in {Gamma,1/Gamma}. Prove the exact stratum ATE interval is min/max of h_1 minus h_0 over the SAME (w_0,w_1), construct endpoint-attaining conditional Bernoulli potential outcomes, and sum over X. Give a complete semialgebraic algorithm enumerating the two exposure-odds boundary arcs and endpoints, analytic outcome-sign branches, and generic interior stationary candidates by resultants, with separate treatment of Gamma=1, constant-U corners, denominator artifacts, and stationary continua. Prove an open-set strict tightening versus the separate-posterior-pair relaxation and characterize the piecewise-algebraic zero-tipping surface. State Manski recovery only as the all-budget limit under vanishing positivity. Certify the rational witness p=1/2,w_1=4/5,w_0=1/5,Gamma_A=16; outcome risks for Y(1)=(13/20,1/20) and Y(0)=(4/5,1/10), with Gamma_0=Gamma_1=36, observed r_1=53/100,r_0=6/25 and causal ATE=-1/10 versus unconfounded ATE=29/100. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: coarse global optimization produced common-U bounds about [-0.1075,0.5395] versus separate-pair bounds about [-0.1104,0.5588]; exact interval arithmetic must certify the gap. At Gamma_A=1 or Gamma_0=Gamma_1=1 the adjusted contrast is point identified; near deterministic U=A recovers Manski in the infinite-budget limit. Credit Rosenbaum–Rubin's fixed-parameter model, VanderWeele–Arah bias decomposition, Ding–VanderWeele arbitrary-U bias factor, Dorn–Guo–Kallus marginal sensitivity bounds, and Nabi et al.'s tilt model. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: rule out missed/spurious resultant roots and verify that Rosenbaum–Rubin Sections 2–4 do not already state an equivalent sharp bounded-parameter envelope. EARLY KILL TEST: use exact rational branch formulas and interval Newton checks on the displayed witness, compare against a direct nonlinear feasibility program and the historical Rosenbaum–Rubin envelope, and stop if any endpoint is missed, the strict gap vanishes, or the novelty collision is exact.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive and exactly certify the sharp covariate-stratum ATE interval and zero-tipping frontier when one shared binary confounder is simultaneously constrained by treatment-confounder and treatment-specific outcome-confounder odds-ratio budgets.

source_refs.claim: Sections 2–4 fix a binary U's prevalence and treatment/outcome log-odds coefficients, invert binary mixtures by a unique quadratic root, and recompute the ATE, but do not optimize a bounded parameter region or prove a sharp envelope.
source_refs.author: Paul R. Rosenbaum and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper gives exact bias decompositions using outcome contrasts and treatment-specific versus marginal confounder distributions, but not sharp bounded-odds optimization with a common binary U.
source_refs.author: Tyler J. VanderWeele and Onyebuchi A. Arah

source_refs.claim: The paper proves sharp marginal-sensitivity ATE bounds and shows that a natural relaxation can remain asymptotically too wide, demonstrating the importance of simultaneous attainability.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn and Kevin Guo
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: There is an open set ... such that the sharp upper endpoint ... is strictly below the rectangular diagnostic envelope.
an exact shared-law two-sided calibration with an attaining-law and verifier certificate
BH-CERT termination at zero weights and active entropy equality is open

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rosenbaum–Rubin supply the fixed-parameter binary-mixture inversion but stop at user-selected tuples and a finite sensitivity grid. The budgeted problem instead requires global optimization over a compact treatment-odds region while both potential-outcome means use the same posterior pair for U; independently optimized armwise extrema need not paste into one causal law. The prior CausalSmith constructions establish analogous strict losses from rectangular or saturated relaxations, but under different polyhedral or entropy restrictions. Here the objective composes exposure-odds boundary arcs with selected quadratic outcome-risk roots: denominator clearing can introduce spurious roots, resultants discard branch inequalities, stationary sets may be positive-dimensional, and Gamma=1 or constant-U corners collapse the generic parameterization. Targeted literature searches found fixed-grid binary-U analyses, arbitrary-U bias factors, and marginal-propensity sensitivity models, but no sharp common-U envelope with a complete degeneracy-aware certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff sharpness theorem expressing each stratum's ATE set as the min/max image of h1(w0,w1)-h0(w0,w1) over one common exposure-odds region, with endpoint-attaining full-data laws, a terminating semialgebraic verifier covering isolated and positive-dimensional stationary sets and all degeneracies, an open-set strict-gap certificate against separate posterior pairs, and a piecewise-algebraic zero-tipping surface.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from an observational-study dispute to one interpretable binary latent covariate and treatment/outcome odds associations is the closest motivation, while the new work can clearly separate bounded-envelope optimization from its fixed-grid calculation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational ATE conclusions depend on ignorability -> posit one binary U restoring conditional ignorability -> calibrate U through treatment and outcome odds associations -> replace fixed-grid recalculation by the exact sharp common-U envelope and tipping frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Invert each binary logistic mixture through its monotone quadratic equation and substitute the feasible latent risks into the standardized potential-outcome mean.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is exactly the local algebra for each fixed shared-U tuple; the new argument must add simultaneous global optimization and constructive sharpness.

method_exemplars.technique: Use least-favorable likelihood-ratio optimization and constructive endpoint arguments to distinguish a sharp sensitivity region from a relaxed armwise envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof exposes precisely why separately plausible armwise extrema may fail simultaneous attainability, although the common-binary-U feasible set is semialgebraic rather than convex-dual.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sharp endpoint functionals with orthogonal scores and prove double validity, double sharpness, efficiency, and Wald coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the population common-U endpoints are characterized, this is the nearest modern template for their regular-stratum estimation and inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct uniformly valid confidence sets for plug-in common-binary-U ATE endpoints and simultaneous confidence regions for the zero-tipping surface across regular branches, optimizer ties, root collisions, and stationary continua.

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs pointwise confidence intervals and confidence bands uniformly valid over a sensitivity-parameter space for a semiparametric latent-confounder model.
source_refs.author: Bo Zhang and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A

source_refs.claim: For fixed sensitivity parameters, the paper derives a nonparametric efficient influence function and a split-sample one-step estimator with root-n asymptotics.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, Ming-Yueh Huang, Marcela Smid, and Daniel O. Scharfstein

source_refs.claim: The paper develops efficient and robust Wald inference for sharp ATE bounds under the marginal sensitivity model, but not for a multibudget algebraic level surface generated by a shared binary U.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn, Kevin Guo, and Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: The exact face-by-face minimax law and an adaptive attaining procedure at dual ties remain open.
Upgrade Conjecture 2 ... to a concrete simultaneous-inference ... theorem
exact normalizations and weak limits ... at regular pairs ... and support-changing contact pairs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoint is a minimum or maximum over algebraic candidates rather than one globally smooth functional. A unique simple root and isolated optimizer permit ordinary influence-function expansion, but ties among arc endpoints and stationary candidates make the endpoint map only directionally differentiable; stationary continua create set-valued active indices, while empirical treatment and outcome risks can also switch the legal quadratic-root branch. The prior IV and entropy proposals identify closely analogous nonregularity at dual ties and support-changing contacts, and the failed QTE proposal was explicitly judged incomplete without simultaneous inference. Existing fixed-parameter influence-function results and sensitivity-indexed confidence bands do not establish uniform coverage over these branch-switch strata or for a multibudget estimated zero level set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem deriving the regular and contact-regime directional limits of both ATE endpoints and the zero-tipping set, together with a derivative-aware bootstrap, multiplier, subsampling, or moment-selection procedure having uniform asymptotic coverage over optimizer ties, root collisions, constant-U contacts, and stationary continua.

writing_exemplar.why: Its breakdown-frontier narrative directly connects assumption relaxation, a sign conclusion, and inference on the boundary where that conclusion ceases to hold.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: scientific conclusions depend on identifying assumptions -> relaxations trace an identified-set path -> the sign changes on a breakdown frontier -> conduct uniform inference on the nonregular common-U zero-tipping surface

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the Hadamard directional derivative of the legal-branch min/max map and use derivative-aware resampling instead of the naive bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoints and tipping map are directionally differentiable min/max functionals at branch ties, exactly where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct sensitivity-indexed asymptotically linear estimators and use their empirical-process limit for confidence bands uniform over a parameter set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired output is likewise a full sensitivity surface, with the additional complication of nonsmooth algebraic branch geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Use efficient influence functions, sample splitting, truncation, and one-step bias correction for a sensitivity-indexed causal effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On each fixed regular branch, a common-U endpoint is a smooth function of observed treatment and outcome risks and can inherit this one-step architecture.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp inclusion, equivalence, and strict-separation relations between the common-binary-U identified set under two-sided treatment and outcome odds budgets and identified sets under marginal propensity-odds and arbitrary-U relative-risk sensitivity models.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives a sharp bias-factor inequality using maximal treatment-confounder and outcome-confounder relative risks without requiring a binary confounder or no interaction.
source_refs.author: Peng Ding and Tyler J. VanderWeele

source_refs.claim: The paper bounds ATE and CATE when latent variables have bounded influence on treatment-assignment odds, but imposes no companion odds budget on U's association with each potential outcome.
source_refs.author: Steve Yadlowsky, Hongseok Namkoong, Sanjay Basu, John Duchi, and Lu Tian

source_refs.claim: The paper emphasizes that sensitivity models can have unintended observable implications and uses Tukey factorization to separate identified from unidentified model components.
source_refs.author: Alexander M. Franks, Alexander D'Amour, and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The models constrain different objects: Ding–VanderWeele bound maximal relative risks over arbitrary U, marginal sensitivity models bound latent-versus-observed treatment odds, and the common-binary-U model bounds an A–U odds ratio plus two Y(a)–U odds ratios while forcing both treatment arms to share one latent prevalence and posterior pair. Converting odds budgets to risk-ratio budgets depends on baseline risks, and discarding shared-U compatibility may enlarge the identified set. Searches located comparisons among marginal sensitivity formulations and discussions of Rosenbaum-type latent models, but no observable-law-dependent sharp translation theorem for this two-sided common-binary restriction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving observable-law-dependent maps between the three budget systems, proving the induced identified-set inclusions, characterizing all equality cases, and supplying rational counterexamples stable on open parameter sets whenever an inclusion is strict.

writing_exemplar.why: Its comparative motivation replaces restrictive binary/no-interaction analyses with a broadly interpretable sharp bias factor, providing a natural template for explaining what is gained and lost by retaining common-binary-U structure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: classical sensitivity analyses impose strong latent structure -> arbitrary-U risk parameters yield a simple sharp bias factor -> simplicity can discard compatibility information from one shared binary U -> derive exact budget translations and strict identified-set comparisons

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce confounding bias to products of outcome contrasts and treatment-induced changes in the distribution of U.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This common algebraic representation places binary-odds and arbitrary-U risk-ratio restrictions on a shared bias scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Use convex duality and conditional quantile balancing to derive an exact extremal distribution under a likelihood-ratio sensitivity constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof distinguishes a sharp model from a relaxation, the same move needed to establish strict inclusion after common-U coupling is removed.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct orthogonal estimators and Wald intervals for sharp sensitivity bounds using a distributionally robust dual representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After a translation theorem identifies comparable budget points, this provides the natural inferential benchmark for empirical comparisons of the intervals.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the sharp joint identified set of benefit and harm probabilities under the same common-binary-confounder treatment and outcome odds budgets, and determine when its coordinatewise or ATE-projection relaxations strictly overcover the jointly attainable region.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sharp symbolic bounds for benefit, no harm, and relative treatment effect under fully confounded observational and imperfect-randomization settings, but not graded common-binary-U odds restrictions.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that the fraction benefiting is generally nonidentified even in randomized trials, derives sharp bounds from potential-outcome marginals, and discusses nonregular inference.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

source_refs.claim: The binary-U sensitivity model targets marginal potential-outcome means and does not constrain the joint distribution of Y(0) and Y(1) required for benefit and harm probabilities.
source_refs.author: Paul R. Rosenbaum and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.excerpt: the exact joint set Theta_kappa(P) of benefit and harm over factual-compatible common-latent SCMs
Neither the scalar programs ... nor the coordinatewise bounds ... address joint-set topology.

open_problems.why_unsolved: ATE sharpness requires only treatment-specific Bernoulli marginals conditional on U, whereas benefit and harm require a joint conditional table for Y(0),Y(1) within each U state. The entropy-budget prior proposal studies joint benefit-harm geometry with an unrestricted finite latent alphabet, but its support reduction relies on entropy structure. Under the destination model, that step must be replaced by a two-state conditional Fréchet-coupling optimization whose marginal risks are themselves selected quadratic roots constrained by one exposure-odds region. Existing benefit-bound papers treat identified marginals or unrestricted confounding; searches found no result combining the joint cross-world target with graded A–U and Y(a)–U odds restrictions on one binary confounder.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp semialgebraic characterization of the attainable pair (P{Y(1)>Y(0)},P{Y(0)>Y(1)}) with explicit within-U endpoint couplings, its exact ATE projection, a finite boundary algorithm, and an open-set witness for strict overcoverage by intersected scalar or separate-arm bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly explains why mean effects can hide who benefits or is harmed and organizes the destination problem around sharp symbolic bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: an average effect can conceal offsetting benefit and harm -> benefit probabilities require the unobserved joint potential-outcome law -> unrestricted confounding gives broad symbolic bounds -> graded common-binary-U odds budgets should yield a sharp intermediate joint set

method_exemplars.technique: Apply extremal copula and Fréchet–Hoeffding arguments to obtain sharp individual-effect distributions from fixed potential-outcome marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional on each U state, the new problem has this marginal-to-joint coupling structure before aggregation over the common latent prevalence.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate response-function types and solve symbolic programs with constructive endpoint laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the destination estimands and endpoint-sharpness logic; the new odds restrictions replace its unrestricted response-type polytope with a semialgebraic feasible set.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate support-restricted benefit bounds through optimization and handle nonregular plug-in behavior with specialized inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The common-U benefit-harm boundary is also an extremum of estimated constraints and inherits active-set and boundary nonregularity.

literature_map:
1. Rosenbaum–Rubin (1983, JRSS B, doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1983.tb01242.x) is the historical anchor: binary A,Y,U, categorical strata, latent conditional ignorability, and fixed prevalence plus treatment/outcome log-odds coefficients.
2. Direct inspection of its Sections 2–4 finds fixed-parameter likelihood calculations: Section 4 derives a unique positive quadratic root for each binary mixture and Section 3 reports 24 sensitivity settings, but no bounded-parameter sharp envelope or tipping-surface optimization.
3. Lin–Psaty–Kronmal (1998, Biometrics, doi:10.2307/2533848) generalize added-confounder regression sensitivity to binary and survival outcomes but remain model-based rather than set-sharp under joint odds budgets.
4. Imbens (2003, AER, doi:10.1257/000282803321946921) reframes Rosenbaum–Rubin sensitivity through calibration and relates sufficiently unrestricted sensitivity to Manski-type bounds.
5. VanderWeele–Arah (2011, Epidemiology, doi:10.1097/EDE.0b013e3181f74493) give an exact general bias decomposition; for binary U it exposes the outcome-contrast times posterior-prevalence-shift structure.
6. Ding–VanderWeele (2016, Epidemiology, arXiv:1507.03984) derive a sharp arbitrary-U relative-risk bias factor, trading binary common-U specificity for broad robustness.
7. Tan (2006, JASA, doi:10.1198/016214506000000023) introduces the marginal sensitivity model bounding latent-versus-nominal propensity odds, a restriction distinct from joint A–U and Y(a)–U odds budgets.
8. Zhao–Small–Bhattacharya (2019, JRSS B, arXiv:1711.11286) give IPW sensitivity bounds and percentile-bootstrap inference; Dorn–Guo subsequently show that the associated population relaxation can be nonsharp.
9. Dorn–Guo (2023, JASA, arXiv:2102.04543) derive sharp marginal-sensitivity bounds by quantile balancing, demonstrating how simultaneous feasibility tightens a natural relaxation.
10. Yadlowsky–Namkoong–Basu–Duchi–Tian (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1808.09521) obtain loss-based ATE/CATE bounds under treatment-odds selection bias without companion outcome-U odds budgets.
11. Dorn–Guo–Kallus (2025, JASA, arXiv:2112.11449) add doubly sharp, doubly valid, efficient estimation and Wald inference for marginal-sensitivity ATE bounds.
12. Franks–D'Amour–Feller (2020, JASA, arXiv:1809.00399) separate identified and unidentified components through Tukey factorization and warn that sensitivity parameterizations can impose unintended observable restrictions.
13. Zhang–Tchetgen Tchetgen (2022, JRSS A, arXiv:1910.14130) provide pointwise intervals and uniform bands over a latent-confounder sensitivity space; Nabi et al. (2024, Biometrics, arXiv:2104.08300) derive efficient one-step inference for fixed tilt parameters.
14. Ciocănea-Teodorescu–Gabriel–Sjölander (2022, Biometrika, doi:10.1093/biomet/asac018) develop variation-independent sensitivity functions and doubly robust estimation for low-level categorical exposures and binary outcomes.
15. Manski (1990, AER P&P, JSTOR:2006592) anchors unrestricted treatment-effect bounds, while Gabriel–Sachs–Jensen (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2305.10555), Fan–Park (2010, Econometric Theory, doi:10.1017/S0266466609990168), and Huang et al. (2017, Biostatistics, doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxw049) delimit adjacent sharp-bound work for benefit and harm.
